ALG-LINEAR-EQ.real_world: Linear equations model real-world scenarios like calculating monthly phone bills (fixed + per-minute charges), converting temperatures between Celsius and Fahrenheit, and predicting travel time based on speed and distance.
ALG-LINEAR-EQ.action: Start with 5 basic slope-intercept problems, then try solving word problems that connect to everyday budgeting scenarios.
flashcard_concepts: y = mx + b → m is slope, b is y-intercept
To solve: isolate the variable using inverse operations

ALG-QUAD-EQ.real_world: Quadratic equations describe projectile motion (how high a ball goes when thrown), the shape of satellite dishes and bridges, and help businesses find the price point that maximizes profit.
ALG-QUAD-EQ.action: First ensure you can factor expressions comfortably, then practice the quadratic formula with real projectile motion problems.
flashcard_concepts: ax² + bx + c = 0 is standard form
Discriminant b²-4ac tells number of solutions
Vertex form: a(x-h)² + k where (h,k) is the turning point

ALG-FACTORING.real_world: Factoring helps simplify complex calculations in physics and engineering — like breaking down forces into components, simplifying circuit equations, and optimizing manufacturing dimensions.
ALG-FACTORING.action: Practice finding GCF of terms first, then move to factoring trinomials using the AC method.
flashcard_concepts: GCF method: find greatest common factor of all terms
Trinomial: find two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b

ALG-POLYNOMIALS.real_world: Polynomials model population growth curves, the trajectory of roller coasters, and are used in computer graphics to create smooth curves and animations in games and movies.
ALG-POLYNOMIALS.action: Start by classifying polynomials by degree, then practice addition and multiplication before attempting division.
flashcard_concepts: Multiply using distributive property (FOIL for binomials)

ALG-FUNCTIONS.real_world: Functions are everywhere — your phone's brightness adjusting to ambient light, Spotify's recommendation algorithm, and how your heart rate responds to exercise intensity are all functions.
ALG-FUNCTIONS.action: Map out input-output tables for daily situations, then practice identifying domain and range from graphs.
flashcard_concepts: Function: each input has exactly one output
Domain = set of valid inputs, Range = set of possible outputs
f(x) notation: f is the rule, x is the input

GEO-TRIANGLES.real_world: Triangles are the strongest shape in engineering — used in bridge trusses, roof structures, crane arms, and even in how GPS satellites triangulate your phone's location.
GEO-TRIANGLES.action: Start with angle-sum property (180°), then practice classifying triangles and using Pythagoras for right triangles.
flashcard_concepts: Pythagoras: a² + b² = c² (right triangles only)
Types: equilateral (60-60-60), isosceles (2 equal), scalene (all different)

GEO-CIRCLES.real_world: Circle geometry is used in wheel and gear design, calculating satellite orbits, designing sports fields and running tracks, and in architecture for domes and arches.
GEO-CIRCLES.action: Memorize key formulas (circumference, area), then practice problems involving arcs, sectors, and tangent lines.
flashcard_concepts: Tangent is perpendicular to radius at point of contact

GEO-COORDINATE.real_world: Coordinate geometry powers Google Maps navigation, drone flight path planning, game character movement systems, and how architects plan building layouts on plots.
GEO-COORDINATE.action: Practice plotting points and finding distances, then move to midpoint formula and equations of lines between points.
flashcard_concepts: Section formula for dividing a line segment

STAT-MEASURES.real_world: Statistics helps you understand cricket batting averages, compare exam performances across schools, analyze Instagram engagement rates, and make sense of COVID data trends.
STAT-MEASURES.action: Practice calculating mean, median, mode on small datasets, then try interpreting which measure best represents real scenarios.
flashcard_concepts: Median = middle value when sorted (average of two middles if even count)
Mean is affected by outliers, median is resistant

STAT-PROBABILITY.real_world: Probability helps predict weather forecasts, assess risk in medical treatments, calculate odds in games, and is the foundation of AI and machine learning predictions.
STAT-PROBABILITY.action: Start with simple single-event probabilities (coins, dice), then progress to combined events and conditional probability.
flashcard_concepts: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)

TRIG-BASIC.real_world: Trigonometry is used in music production (sound waves), measuring building heights without climbing them, in video game physics for character animations, and in navigation by ships and aircraft.
TRIG-BASIC.action: Master SOH-CAH-TOA with right triangle diagrams first, then practice finding angles and sides in real measurement problems.
flashcard_concepts: SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic, works for right triangles only

TRIG-IDENTITIES.real_world: Trig identities simplify complex calculations in electrical engineering (AC circuits), signal processing (noise reduction in audio), and physics (wave interference patterns).
TRIG-IDENTITIES.action: Start by proving sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 geometrically, then practice simplifying expressions using basic identities before attempting proofs.
flashcard_concepts: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
